label: rem:no-global-section
title: Remark
body_md:
\relax{rem:no-global-section}
The bundle $\mathrm{SO}(3) \to S^2$ is the unit tangent bundle of the sphere: a section is a choice of unit tangent vector at every point, and by the hairy-ball theorem no such choice is continuous.  The section \eqref{eq:section}, which follows the meridians away from the poles, is measurable but not continuous.  The intrinsic spin-field constructions below are independent of this choice, with their coordinate expressions related by \eqref{eq:section-change}; the mixed-spin section evaluations of Sec.~\relax{sec:beyond:section} instead depend on the chosen section and do not transform by one common spin phase.  For continuous spin fields, the limiting coordinate values at the poles vanish or carry the windings $e^{\mp\mathrm{i} s\varphi}$ \relax{boyle2016how,mcewen2011novel}; bare $L^2$ classes have no intrinsic point values there.

label: lem:twist-composition
title: Lemma
body_md:
\relax{lem:twist-composition}
$\hbar(x, g_1 g_2) = \hbar(g_2 x, g_1)\, \hbar(x, g_2)$ for all $x \in G/H$ and $g_1, g_2 \in G$.  On the sphere, with the section \eqref{eq:section}, $\hbar(R(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)) = R_z(\gamma)$ for $0<\beta<\pi$, hence almost everywhere.
head: environment
name: Composition of twists

title: Proof
body_md: The composition rule follows by inserting $s(g_2x)\,s(g_2x)^{-1}$ into $s(g_1g_2x)^{-1}g_1g_2s(x)$ and regrouping (it is Eq.~(20) of \relax{cohen2019general}).  On the sphere, for $0<\beta<\pi$, $s(R(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\eta) = R(\alpha,\beta,0)$, hence $\hbar(R(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)) = R(\alpha,\beta,0)^{-1}R(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = R_z(\gamma)$.  The details are given in Appendix~\relax{app:proofs}.

label: rem:spin-fields-are-sections
title: Remark
body_md:
\relax{rem:spin-fields-are-sections}
The identification just made is the bridge between the physics and the bundle literatures.  The spin-weighted quantities of Newman \& Penrose \relax{newman1966note} and Goldberg \mbox{\it et al.}\ \relax{goldberg1967spin}, defined by their behaviour \eqref{eq:spin-phase} under a rotation of the local frame and adopted for the polarisation of the cosmic microwave background in \relax{zaldarriaga1997all,kamionkowski1997statistics}, are the sections of the line bundle associated to $\mathrm{SO}(3) \to S^2$ by the character $\rho^{(s)}$, and their coordinate expression depends on the choice of frame exactly as \eqref{eq:section-change} prescribes.  Boyle \relax{boyle2016how} draws the same conclusion from the impossibility of a global frame, noting that spin-weighted functions are not functions on the sphere alone but functions of a point together with a frame at that point, \mbox{\it i.e.}\ functions on the rotation group; the general theory of such coordinate-independent fields on manifolds is developed by Weiler \mbox{\it et al.}\ \relax{weiler2021coordinate}.  On the sphere the oriented orthonormal frame bundle is $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, which is distinct from a chosen local frame field.  Note that the encoding as a Mackey function is global and involves no choice of section, whereas the encoding as a spin field does; the former is therefore the natural setting in which to establish properties such as equivariance, and the latter the natural setting in which to compute.

label: lem:lift
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Structure of the lift

title: Proof
body_md: We outline the proof; the details are given in Appendix~\relax{app:proofs}.  Part (a) follows from Fubini's theorem and the Fourier series of $F$ in the fibre coordinate $\gamma$, of which $\Lambda_{s}\Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}F$ is the term in $e^{-\mathrm{i} s\gamma}$.  Part (b) is immediate from \eqref{eq:Ms}.  Part (d) is the relation \eqref{eq:sY-D} between spin spherical harmonics and Wigner functions, together with their orthogonality, and (c) follows from (d) by linearity: by \eqref{eq:D-sY} and the orthogonality of the complex exponentials, the Wigner coefficients of $\Lambda_{s}f$ vanish unless $n = -s$, and $\int_0^{2\pi} e^{-\mathrm{i}(s+n)\gamma}\,\mathrm{d}\gamma = 2\pi\delta_{n,-s}$ supplies the constant.  Part (e) is Proposition~\relax{prop:intertwining} below.

label: rem:evaluation
title: Remark
body_md:
\relax{rem:evaluation}
Cohen, Geiger \& Weiler \relax{cohen2019general} and Xu \mbox{\it et al.}\ \relax{xu2022unified} define the inverse of the unnormalised lift on Mackey functions by evaluation on the section, $F\mapsto F\circ s$, which by (b) equals $\Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ on $\mathcal{M}_{s}$.  Xu \mbox{\it et al.}\ also define a general convolutional projection $P^\kappa$ on group functions and implement a fixed fibre integral after the nonlinearity; with their unnormalised stabiliser measure this integral is $\sqrt{2\pi}\,\Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}$ and is not restricted to Mackey functions.  Kondor \& Trivedi \relax{kondor2018generalization} use the scalar fibre average.  We adopt the adjoint convention throughout: it is bounded on all of $L^2(\mathrm{SO}(3))$, selects a definite output spin equivariantly for arbitrary kernels, and, with the isometric lift, satisfies $\Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}\Lambda_{s}=\operatorname{Id}$.  The degree-dependent factors also cancel under section evaluation on a constrained range; the adjoint provides a consistent normalisation, with the constants of the classical reductions tracked explicitly in Sec.~\relax{sec:reductions}.  The forthcoming article \relax{mulder2026spin} adopts the same convention.

label: rem:phase-interpretation
title: Remark
body_md:
\relax{rem:phase-interpretation}
The rotation $R_\rho^{-1}$ carries the reference frame $s(x)$ at $x$ to a frame at $R_\rho^{-1}x$ that differs from the chosen frame there by $\hbar(x,R_\rho^{-1})=R_z(\vartheta)$ (Fig.~\relax{fig:twist}).  The phase $e^{-\mathrm{i} s\vartheta}$ is the character $\rho^{(s)}$ evaluated on the inverse twist.  This residual frame rotation is already described in the spin-wavelet treatment \relax{mcewen2015directional} and by Boyle \relax{boyle2016how}; Proposition~\relax{prop:intertwining} connects those conventions to the induced-action formula of Cohen, Geiger \& Weiler \relax{cohen2019general}.  The common harmonic law \eqref{eq:rotation-coeffs} then follows because $\Lambda_{s}$ intertwines $\mathcal{R}_\rho$ with left translation on $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, which acts on the first Wigner index by the same $D^\ell$ for every spin.
head: environment
name: Geometric meaning of the spin rotation phase

label: cor:fibre-decomposition
title: Corollary
body_md:
\relax{cor:fibre-decomposition}
Every $F \in L^2(\mathrm{SO}(3))$ decomposes uniquely as $F = \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}} \Lambda_{s}\Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}F$, its Fourier series in $\gamma$ converging in $L^2$, with $(\Lambda_{s}\Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}F)^{\ell}_{mn} = F^{\ell}_{mn}\,\delta_{n,-s}$; the component $\Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}F$ is a spin-$s$ field whose harmonic coefficients are the Wigner column $F^{\ell}_{m,-s}$ up to the constant in \eqref{eq:lift-harmonic}.  In particular $F$ is azimuthally band-limited at $N$, $F^{\ell}_{mn} = 0$ for $\lvert n \rvert \ge N$, if and only if $F = \sum_{\lvert s \rvert < N} \Lambda_{s} f_s$ for spin fields $f_s = \Lambda_{s}^{\dagger}F$.

title: Proof
body_md: By Lemma~\relax{lem:lift}(c) the Wigner coefficients of the lifted field are supported on the single column $m' = -s$, so that the sum over $m'$ in \eqref{eq:group-conv-harmonic} collapses to a single term and \eqref{eq:harmonic-sG} follows; applying $\Lambda_{s'}^{\dagger}$ by \eqref{eq:lift-harmonic} reads the column $n = -s'$ and multiplies by $(-1)^{s'}\sqrt{(2\ell+1)/8\pi^2}$, so that the degree-dependent constants cancel and \eqref{eq:harmonic-ss} follows, while \eqref{eq:harmonic-Gs} is $\Lambda_{s'}^{\dagger}$ applied to \eqref{eq:group-conv-harmonic}.  Equivariance follows since $\Lambda_{s}$, $\Lambda_{s'}^{\dagger}$ and $\Psi\star$ each intertwine the relevant representations, by Lemma~\relax{lem:lift}(e) and the left invariance of the Haar measure, and the adjoint identities follow from Fubini's theorem, the adjoint of $\Psi\star$ being $\widetilde\Psi\star$.  The details are given in Appendix~\relax{app:proofs}.

title: Proof

title: Proof
body_md: The equivalence of (i) and (ii) follows from \eqref{eq:harmonic-sG} and the characterisation of $\mathcal{M}_{s'}$ as the column $n = -s'$ of Wigner space (Lemma~\relax{lem:lift}); that of (ii) and (iii) by expanding $\Psi^{(s)}$ in Wigner functions and noting that $D^{\ell *}_{mn}(R_z(\chi_1)gR_z(\chi_2)) = e^{\mathrm{i} m\chi_1}D^{\ell *}_{mn}(g)e^{\mathrm{i} n\chi_2}$. label: thm:classification
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Classification

title: Proof
body_md: By Frobenius reciprocity the multiplicity of the degree-$\ell$ irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ in $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\rho^{(s)}$ equals the multiplicity of $\rho^{(s)}$ in its restriction to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, which is one if $\ell \ge \lvert s\rvert$ and zero otherwise, so that $L^2_{s}(S^2)$ decomposes without multiplicity into the subspaces spanned by the $\prescript{}{s}{Y}_{\ell m}$, $\lvert m\rvert \le \ell$, on which $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ acts by the same matrices $D^{\ell}$ for every spin by \eqref{eq:rotation-coeffs}.  Schur's lemma then forces $T$ to map each such subspace to its counterpart of the same degree by a scalar $c_\ell$, and to annihilate degrees absent from the target; boundedness of $T$ is equivalent to $\sup_\ell \lvert c_\ell\rvert < \infty$.  Part (a) follows by comparing \eqref{eq:harmonic-ss} with \eqref{eq:classification} and computing $\lVert\Psi_T\rVert^2 = \sum_\ell\frac{2\ell+1}{8\pi^2}\lvert c_\ell\rvert^2$, part (b) by extending $\Psi\star$ to distributional kernels with bounded Wigner coefficients, and part (c) by the same argument applied to the left regular representation, in which the degree-$\ell$ representation occurs with multiplicity $2\ell+1$, one copy per column.  Parseval's identity weights each Wigner block by $a_\ell$, whereas the spin harmonic coefficients have unit weight, giving the norms \eqref{eq:classification-norms}.  The details are given in Appendix~\relax{app:proofs}.

label: cor:projection-general
title: Corollary
body_md:
\relax{cor:projection-general}
Every bounded $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-equivariant linear map $L^2(\mathrm{SO}(3)) \to L^2_{s'}(S^2)$ is $\mathcal{C}_{G\to s'}[\Psi]$ for a kernel (in general a distribution) whose only nonzero row is $n=-s'$ in each degree $\ell\ge\lvert s'\rvert$.  If the map acts by $(TF)_{\ell m}=\sum_{m'}c^\ell_{m'}F^\ell_{mm'}$, then $c^\ell_{m'}=(-1)^{s'}\sqrt{(2\ell+1)/(8\pi^2)}\,\Psi^{\ell *}_{-s',m'}$, subject to \eqref{eq:classification-norms}.  The adjoint projection $\Lambda_{s'}^{\dagger}$ is the case $\Psi^{\ell *}_{-s',m'}=\delta_{m',-s'}$, which reads one Wigner column.  Dually, every bounded equivariant map $L^2_{s}(S^2) \to L^2(\mathrm{SO}(3))$ is $\mathcal{C}_{s\to G}[\Psi]$ for a kernel with a single column $m'=-s$, and $\Lambda_{s}$ is the case $\Psi^{\ell *}_{n,-s}=\delta_{n,-s}$.

label: prop:section-evaluation

head: environment
name: Evaluation on a section

title: Proof
body_md: Corollary~\relax{cor:fibre-decomposition} and Definition~\relax{def:lift} give the finite sum, which is bounded since each component is bounded and the phase has unit modulus.  If it is equivariant into spin $t$, Theorem~\relax{thm:classification} applies.  Testing each input harmonic and comparing the independent Wigner columns representing the different output spins forces all components except $t$ to vanish and, for a nonzero map, forces its phase to be constant almost everywhere.  The converse follows from equivariance of $\mathcal{C}_{s\to t}$.  Polar rotations act by coordinate rotation for every spin; substituting $\chi_\sigma=\pi-\varphi$ gives the stated phase criterion.  The degreewise argument and the zero-map case are detailed in Appendix~\relax{app:proofs:beyond}.

label: prop:diagonal
title: Proposition
body_md:
\relax{prop:diagonal}
Let $T$ act on $L^2(S^2)$ by $(Tf)_{\ell m}=g_{\ell m}f_{\ell m}$ with a bounded coefficient sequence $g$.  This is harmonic multiplication, or sifting with the coefficientwise-conjugated filter; the filter may be a distribution.  Then $T$ commutes with every polar rotation, and is $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-equivariant if and only if $g_{\ell m}$ is independent of $m$ for each $\ell$.  In that case $T=\mathcal{C}_{0\to 0}[\Psi_T]$ with $c_\ell=g_{\ell0}$ in the Fourier-multiplier sense of Theorem~\relax{thm:classification}, with a generally distributional zonal representative.  If $g_{\ell m}=g_{\ell,-m}$, $T$ also commutes with $R_y(\pi)$, and thus with the embedded $O(2)$ normaliser of polar rotations.

body_md: By \eqref{eq:harmonic-sG} the Wigner coefficients of $\mathcal{C}_{s\to G}[\Psi]f$ vanish for $\lvert n\rvert \ge N$ when the column $m' = -s$ of $\Psi$ does.  Corollary~\relax{cor:fibre-decomposition} applied to the output gives $\mathcal{C}_{s\to G}[\Psi]f = \sum_{\lvert s'\rvert<N}\Lambda_{s'}\Lambda_{s'}^{\dagger}\mathcal{C}_{s\to G}[\Psi]f$, and $\Lambda_{s'}^{\dagger}\mathcal{C}_{s\to G}[\Psi] = \mathcal{C}_{s\to s'}[\Psi]$ by Definition~\relax{def:lifted-conv}.  Conversely, given at most $2N-1$ bounded multipliers $c^{(s')}_\ell$, the canonical column $\Psi^{\ell}_{-s',-s}=(-1)^{s+s'}c^{(s')*}_{\ell}$ defines a distribution and assembles the tuple by the same identity.  The norm bound is $\sup_\ell(\sum_{s'}\lvert c^{(s')}_\ell\rvert^2)^{1/2}<\infty$.  By Parseval, the kernel belongs to $L^2$ exactly when $\sum_{\ell,s'}(2\ell+1)\lvert c^{(s')}_\ell\rvert^2<\infty$, the sum of the component Hilbert--Schmidt norms squared.  This condition holds automatically at finite band-limit.

body_md: For a rotation $R_z(a)$ about the polar axis the twist vanishes, so that $(\pi_{0}(R_z(a))f)_{\ell m} = e^{-\mathrm{i} ma}f_{\ell m}$ by \eqref{eq:rotation-coeffs} and \eqref{eq:wignerD}; a diagonal multiplier commutes with this action for every $g_{\ell m}$.  Equivariance under all of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ is, by Theorem~\relax{thm:classification} with $s = s' = 0$, the condition that $T$ act by a scalar on each degree, \mbox{\it i.e.}\ that $g_{\ell m}$ be independent of $m$, in which case $T$ is the axisymmetric convolution $\mathcal{C}_{0\to 0}[\Psi_T]$ with $c_\ell = g_{\ell 0}$, understood in the distributional multiplier sense.  Moreover, $D^\ell(R_y(\pi))$ exchanges $m$ and $-m$ up to the nonzero sign in \eqref{eq:app-d-poles}, so it commutes with the diagonal multiplier when $g_{\ell m}=g_{\ell,-m}$.  Together with the polar rotations this gives the embedded $O(2)$ normaliser.
